title: A Message to You, Rudy
whyNotable: The 2 Tone anthem is assumed to be a Specials original, but Dandy Livingstone wrote and recorded it in London in 1967; Rico Rodriguez played the trombone intro on both his version and the Specials' 1979 remake.

title: Babe I'm Gonna Leave You
whyNotable: Written by Anne Bredon in the late 1950s; the first published recording was Joan Baez's 1962 in-concert album, credited there only as traditional. Zeppelin's 1969 debut credited it 'Traditional, arr. Jimmy Page' until Bredon approached the band and won credit plus back royalties in 1990.

title: Beyond the Sea
writer: Charles Trenet (French original 'La Mer'); Jack Lawrence (English lyrics)
whyNotable: Trenet's 'La Mer' was published in 1946, but the first recording was made by Roland Gerbeau in December 1945, ahead of Trenet's own. Jack Lawrence's English lyric turned an ode to the sea into a love song; Darin's Atco single did not appear until January 1960.

title: Bring It On Home
whyNotable: Recorded by Sonny Boy Williamson II on 11 January 1963 for Checker and released in 1966. Zeppelin's Led Zeppelin II track opened and closed with deliberate quotations of it; Chess publisher Arc Music sued, the band settled, and later reissues give Willie Dixon sole songwriting credit.

title: Cry Baby
whyNotable: Garnet Mimms took it to No. 1 R&B and No. 4 pop in 1963, but Joplin's posthumous Pearl version is so identified with her that Mimms has largely vanished from the song's story.

title: Dazed and Confused
whyNotable: Holmes wrote and recorded it for his 1967 debut album; Led Zeppelin's 1969 debut credited it to Jimmy Page alone. Holmes sued Page in 2010, the case was dismissed with prejudice in January 2012 after a settlement, and later releases changed the credit to 'By Page - Inspired by Jake Holmes'.

title: Delta Dawn
whyNotable: Co-writer Alex Harvey recorded it first, on his November 1971 Capitol album; Tanya Tucker's April 1972 Columbia country hit came next, and Helen Reddy's June 1973 pop version - a US No. 1 - is the one most people name.

title: Don't Turn Around
whyNotable: Twice mistaken: Ace of Base's 1994 hit is usually taken as theirs, and those who know better usually credit Aswad's 1988 UK No. 1 reggae version - but the first recording was Tina Turner's, issued in 1986 as the B-side of 'Typical Male'.

title: Everybody Needs Somebody to Love
writer: Bert Berns, Solomon Burke and Jerry Wexler
whyNotable: Solomon Burke co-wrote and recorded it on 28 May 1964, released that July on Atlantic; the 1980 Blues Brothers film performance is now the default reference point for a whole generation. The Rolling Stones had already covered it in January 1965.

title: Everybody's Talkin'
whyNotable: The textbook sync case: Nilsson's 1968 recording flopped as a single, then Midnight Cowboy made it a hit so total that the song is now subtitled 'Theme from Midnight Cowboy'. Fred Neil wrote and recorded it first, on his self-titled Capitol album released December 1966.
